data.content:
A `-` prefix now subtracts, and works on tags and tiers alike:

```bash
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE="-ga"          # every locale except Irish
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE="primary,-hu"  # en-AU, en-CA, en-GB
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE="-secondary"   # equivalent to primary
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE="-ga,-he"      # multiple exclusions
```

A value made only of exclusions starts from the full locale set; exclusions applied to an explicit selection just narrow it. The "only subtractions start from everything" rule is keyed on whether any positive entry was *given*, not on whether it expanded to anything — otherwise `DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE=source` (a tier no docs locale belongs to) would have silently translated all 44 locales instead of throwing. A selection that ends up empty, including `"hu,-hu"`, throws.

But if it's *still* hanging past 120s, the timeout wasn't the whole story — I found a second bug and fixed it in [tools/translation-adapters/src/index.ts](tools/translation-adapters/src/index.ts):

`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND` points at `copilot-wrapper.sh`, so the child Node kills is **bash**, not `copilot`. `child.kill("SIGKILL")` reaped the shell and left `copilot` orphaned — still holding the inherited stdout pipe, which keeps Node's handle open and the run wedged even after the promise rejects. The child is now spawned with `detached: true` and the timeout signals the whole process group (`process.kill(-pid)`), with a fallback to the direct kill if the group is already gone. Two tests cover both paths.

To confirm which unit it's stuck on, run just that locale with verbose bounds:

```bash
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE=ga DOCS_TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT_MS=45000 DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY=1 \
DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=ai \
DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tools/translation-adapters/copilot-wrapper.sh" \
DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS="--model gpt-5-mini --effort low" node scripts/build-api-locales.ts
```

Concurrency 1 makes the failing chunk unambiguous, and a 45s bound surfaces it fast. If you have an old run still going, kill any stray `copilot` processes (`pgrep -fl copilot`) before restarting — those are the orphans from before this fix.
